text.p: Agribusiness firm Andersons Inc said Tuesday the year's bad weather and corn crop situation are dampening its grain elevator business.
But the Maumee, Ohio-based firm's fertilizer, lawn care and railcar businesses are doing well and its retail business is improving, its top officers said in a telephone interview.

In 1995, Maumee, Ohio-based Andersons earned $0.74 a share on $1.1 billion revenues. It has operations in Ohio, Michigan, Indiana and Illinois, a region hit by a wet spring and dry weather later in the growing season.
"(The weather) will have a negative impact on the storage business in our area," President Mike Anderson said.

Low carryover of corn available from last year plus strong demand and available on-farm storage for this year's crop mean less demand for Andersons' 67 million bushels of grain elevator storage space, he said.
But with the late harvest yet to come in, "we're hoping to fill it," Chairman and Chief Executive Dick Anderson said.
Both said that after two rough crop years in a row, they are optimistic about 1997, assuming normal yields next year.
About 60 percent of 1995 revenues came from the grain business including grain elevators.
They declined to make earnings projections.

The Andersons, which plans to report its third quarter about Novenber 7, historically has "difficult" first and third quarters and strong second and fourth quarters, Gary Smith, vice president, finance, said in the same interivew.
Mark Koprucki, an analyst with Ohio Co, said he estimates 1996 earnings will be $0.85 a share.
The Andersons went public in February.

Its agricultural fertilizer business improved this year over 1995, Dick Anderson said. "We project a good close on our wholesale fertilizer business. Fertilizer's been steady for us and the outlook is good." He hopes for "a booming agricultural fertilizer year" in 1997, particularly since it will be a year unfettered by U.S. government acreage controls, he said.
The Andersons' rail car repair, sale and leasing business "is growing fast and is very profitable," Dick Anderson said, adding it will contribute substantially to before-tax income.
This year Andersons' lawn care business, selling products to mass retailers, is ahead of plan and ahead of 1995 "and we look forward to another good (year in 1997)."
He said Andersons has improved its raw materials purchasing, especially of nitrogen, whose volatile pricing hurt that unit's operating profits in 1994-95.

Its retail group of six home center/specialty foods stores is "doing a lot better this year," the chairman said. Its Columbus, Ohio, stores are locked in a "battle royal" with home-center competitors, but he said those two stores will be redesigned next year, based on a successful Toledo store.
Dick Anderson, 67, said he expects his nephew Mike, 45, to succeed him as chief executive officer, possibly in two to three years.
